claim: Heliomycin and 4-dmH engage and target SIRT1 in p53-functional SAS oral cancer cells
source: In this study, we conducted cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA) and molecular docking simulations to identify and validate that heliomycin and its water-soluble derivative, 4-(dimethylaminomethyl)heliomycin (designated compound 4-dmH) engaged and targeted with sirtuin-1 (SIRT1) in p53-functional SAS and p53-mutated HSC-3 oral cancer cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by CETSA data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Heliomycin and 4-dmH engage and target SIRT1 in p53-mutated HSC-3 oral cancer cells
source: In this study, we conducted cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA) and molecular docking simulations to identify and validate that heliomycin and its water-soluble derivative, 4-(dimethylaminomethyl)heliomycin (designated compound 4-dmH) engaged and targeted with sirtuin-1 (SIRT1) in p53-functional SAS and p53-mutated HSC-3 oral cancer cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by CETSA data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: 4-dmH preferentially targets tNOX (ENOX2) in addition to SIRT1
source: We further addressed the cellular outcome of SIRT1 inhibition by these compounds and found that, in addition to SIRT1, the water-soluble 4-dmH preferentially targeted a tumor-associated NADH oxidase (tNOX, ENOX2).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by CETSA data in Figure 8.

claim: Direct binding of 4-dmH to tNOX decreases the oxidation of NADH to NAD+
source: The direct binding of 4-dmH to tNOX decreased the oxidation of NADH to NAD+ which diminished NAD+-dependent SIRT1 deacetylase activity, ultimately inducing apoptosis and significant cytotoxicity in both cell types, as opposed to the parental heliomycin-induced autophagy.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by NAD+/NADH ratio measurements in Figure 7a.

claim: 4-dmH binding to tNOX diminishes NAD+-dependent SIRT1 deacetylase activity

evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by SIRT1 activity assays in Figure 4a and NAD+/NADH ratio data in Figure 7a.

claim: 4-dmH functions through targeting the tNOX-NAD+-SIRT1 axis to induce apoptosis in oral cancer cells
source: Taken together, our in vitro and in vivo findings suggest that the multifaceted properties of water-soluble 4-dmH enable it to offer superior antitumor value compared to parental heliomycin, and indicated that it functions through targeting the tNOX-NAD+-SIRT1 axis to induce apoptosis in oral cancer cells.

evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citation to Chueh et al., 2002.

claim: The binding site of the studied compounds on tNOX is located well away from the NADH-binding motif
source: However, our simulation results indicated that the binding site of the studied compounds is located well away from the NADH-binding motif of the tNOX protein.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on molecular docking simulations.

claim: The consistent interacting residues involved in the hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions of the studied compounds with tNOX were predicted to be Ile90, Lys98, Pro111, Pro113, Leu115, Pro117, and Pro118
source: The consistent interacting residues involved in the hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions of the studied compounds were predicted to be Ile90, Lys98, Pro111, Pro113, Leu115, Pro117, and Pro118 (Figure 9D), which are not located in the NADH-binding motif.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on molecular docking simulations shown in Figure 9D.

claim: The superior anticancer activity of 4-dmH over its parental heliomycin resides in its direct targeting of tNOX and SIRT1
source: Taken together, our present results show that the superior anticancer activity of 4-dmH over its parental heliomycin resides in its direct targeting of tNOX and SIRT1, and suggest that the tNOX-NAD+-SIRT1 regulatory axis contributes to inducing apoptosis independent of p53 status, as evidenced by the results of in vitro and in vivo studies of oral cancer.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary conclusion.

claim: The tNOX-NAD+-SIRT1 regulatory axis contributes to inducing apoptosis independent of p53 status
source: Taken together, our present results show that the superior anticancer activity of 4-dmH over its parental heliomycin resides in its direct targeting of tNOX and SIRT1, and suggest that the tNOX-NAD+-SIRT1 regulatory axis contributes to inducing apoptosis independent of p53 status, as evidenced by the results of in vitro and in vivo studies of oral cancer.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary conclusion.

claim: The tNOX- and SIRT1-inhibiting function of 4-dmH results in different biological outcomes from the SIRT1-binding heliomycin
source: Considering that tNOX not only supports but also exerts functions independent of SIRT1, the tNOX- and SIRT1-inhibiting function of 4-dmH, thus, results in the different biological outcomes from the SIRT1-binding heliomycin, as evidenced by the results of in vitro and in vivo studies of oral cancer.
evidence: This is stated in the conclusions section as a summary statement.
